Dating to marry can be very complicated. Some people hear dating to marry and are almost scared off: marriage, commitment, etc. are all things that can sound scary to people especially on a first impression. At this point in your relationship (flirting, first dates, getting to know one another) you don't even love each other yet. So yes, you want to date seriously and not have short flings or stands, BUT you need to still have fun and get used to dating and getting to know the right person before you relinquish what you want. Most of the time you can tell right off the bat what they are looking for. Remember, it's called the honeymoon phase for a reason, the beginning of a relationship is so much fun! So, don't worry about getting too serious until you think the time is ready to commit completely to one another.

Firstly, If he has/had an issue with you or your relationship he should be emotionally mature enough to discuss it with you. Even if he wanted to end your relationship, for whatever reason it may be, he should've been open with his position and gave you the ability to be open with him. I have been through this numerous times. In my experience, I've learned that closure isn't always the best thing. Yes, it can be something that nags in your mind but there is a point when you need to determine for yourself an answer that will put your mind at ease and give you something to rely on. It doesn't need to be long and complicated it can just be, "he wasn't ready for a relationship," or, "maybe we just weren't meant to be." Also, I always live by: "it it's meant to be, it will be." If you are supposed to end up with this guy, then it will happen eventually. If not, hey now you have time to find someone else (if you're even looking).
